title: Every human vanished tonight. You're the only witness.
sources: docs/quellen-erde-ohne-menschen.md

style.why: Zeitleisten-Thema mit Karten, Diagrammen (Abklingbecken, Orbit, Höhen-Lineal) und Zähler: flache 2D-Infografik erklärt das am klarsten und entspricht dem Format der Inspirationsvideos; düstere Nachtpalette mit gelbem Akzent trägt den Thriller-Ton.
style.characters: YOU = blass-cyaner Geist (runder Kopf, hohle Augen, gelbes Halstuch als einziges Gelb neben den Stadtlichtern), in jeder Szene sichtbar; keine weiteren Menschen nach dem Hook.

note: Themen-Art: Gedankenexperiment/Weltraum+Natur. Klammer: YOU ist der letzte Zeuge (Geist) und hat eine Frage: 'how long until this planet forgets we were ever here?' (Hook, Re-Hook in 'swift' bei ~40 %, Antwort im Wendepunkt 'moon': Erde vergisst langsam, der Mond nicht). HUD: großer Zähler TIME oben links mit Text-Werten (HOUR 0 → HOUR 1 → DAY 1 → DAY 2 → WEEK 1 → MONTH 1 → YEAR 1 → YEAR 10 → YEAR 15 → YEAR 25 → YEAR 300 → YEAR 1,000 → YEAR 10,000), darunter Balken HUMAN TRACES (sinkt, friert beim Mond ein). Szenen 'blackout' und 'comeback' sind als Vorschau/Analogie markiert (heutige Ereignisse mit Menschen). Loop: letzte Worte 'And it all starts tonight.' → erster Satz 'Tonight, every human on Earth vanishes.' Zahlen ausgeschrieben (Chatterbox), Sticker mit Ziffern. Hinweis Szenenbau: Zähler-Wert ist ein String – falls das HUD nur Zahlen kann, Text-Zähler im 2D-Kit bauen.

scenes.text: Tonight, every human on Earth *vanishes*. Everyone. Except you. You're a ghost now, the last witness. And you get one question: | how long until this planet *forgets* we were ever here?
scenes.visual: 2D flat, deep navy night. Big counter top-left 'HOUR 0', thin progress bar under it at 0 %. A busy street in flat paper-cut style: people mid-step, then POP, empty clothes drop, phones fall. YOU = pale-cyan ghost (round head, hollow eyes, little scarf in signal yellow) fades in alone among the piles, looks at camera on 'forgets'.
sources: Gedankenexperiment, keine Faktenaussage (Prämisse)

scenes.text: Zoom out. From space, Earth's night side still *twinkles* with our cities. A NOAA scientist said nothing tells us more about the spread of humans across the Earth than *city lights*. | Enjoy the view.
scenes.visual: Whip up from the street to orbit: flat 2D Earth night side, yellow city dots in clusters (Black-Marble look, stylised). YOU floats in front of the globe like a tiny astronaut-ghost. Quote card slides in (small, upper half). On 'change' one cluster flickers.
sources: Z4: "The night side of our planet twinkles with light, and the first thing to stand out is the cities."
Z5: "Nothing tells us more about the spread of humans across the Earth than city lights," (Chris Elvidge, NOAA)

scenes.text: Here's a preview. In April twenty twenty-five, a blackout hit Spain. Trains *stopped*. Hospitals ran on generators. Phones died. The south stayed dark all night, and that was *with* crews fixing it. Tonight? | Nobody's coming.
scenes.visual: Counter flips to 'HOUR 1'. Flat map of Spain, power lines as glowing strokes going dark south to north; icons pop: halted train, hospital with generator, phone with no bars. YOU checks a dead phone. Cut: empty repair truck with open door, nobody inside, on 'Nobody'.
sources: Z1: "A widespread power outage on April 28, 2025" · "Trains came to a halt, hospitals relied on generators, and phone and internet connections failed."
Z2: "But in the country's south, darkness lasted through at least the night."
"Nobody's coming" = Gedankenexperiment-Folgerung (Quellendatei Z1: Folgerung, keine Zahl)

scenes.text: After a hurricane knocked out Puerto Rico's grid, satellite images showed the dark. Now picture that *everywhere*. No crews. City by city, the lights go out.
scenes.visual: Counter 'DAY 1'. Split frame: small satellite photo-style panel of San Juan with dark patches, then the big flat globe from scene 2: yellow dots switch off in waves, sweeping west. YOU watches from orbit, his scarf the only yellow left.
sources: Z3: "Most of the electric power grid and telecommunications network was knocked offline." · "The images above show widespread outages around San Juan"
"City by city" = Gedankenexperiment ohne Zeitangabe (Quellendatei Fallen: keine Stundenzahl)

scenes.text: And then something comes *back*. Light pollution hides the Milky Way from more than a third of humanity. Without us, the sky goes *full blast*. | Best show ever. Zero audience.
scenes.visual: Counter 'DAY 2'. Ground level, dark empty city skyline in flat silhouettes; the sky fills layer by layer with stars, then the Milky Way band in soft 2D gradient. YOU lies on a car roof, alone, applauding slowly on 'Zero audience'.
sources: Z23: "The Milky Way is hidden from more than one-third of humanity" (Falchi et al. 2016)
"sky goes full blast" = Folgerung, in Quellendatei Z23 als Folgerung erlaubt

scenes.text: Meanwhile, at nuclear plants, used fuel still makes *heat*. It cools in pools under about *twenty feet* of water, giving operators time to fix any problem. | Operators. Right. Other fuel sits in dry casks. No fans, no pumps, about the heat of a home heater. Cozy.
scenes.visual: Counter 'WEEK 1'. Cutaway diagram (flat infographic): blue pool, fuel racks at the bottom, a '20 FT' measuring line. Empty control room chair spins slowly on 'Operators'. Then a row of grey casks with little arrow streams of warm air rising; YOU warms his ghost hands at one on 'Cozy'.
sources: Z18: "spent fuel still produces a lot of radiation and heat that must be managed" · "about 20 feet of water above the top of the fuel, giving plant operators time to correct any problem that may arise."
Z19: "without fans or pumps" · "A typical cask emits roughly the same heat as a home-heating system."
Keine Aussage über Schmelze/Unfall (Quellendatei Fallen)

scenes.text: Look up. The satellites still fly. For now. Dodging each other is routine, and someone has to steer. | Nobody steers. And the Sun heats our air, it puffs up, and drag pulls them *lower*.
scenes.visual: Counter 'MONTH 1'. Orbit view, flat: satellites as white icons on dotted tracks; two drift close, a red warning ring pulses, no hand on the joystick in a tiny empty ops room inset. Then the atmosphere drawn as a glowing layer swelling outward; satellites dip down a notch.
sources: Z25: "Collision avoidance ... is now a regular part of flying missions in low-Earth orbit." (ESA)
Z6: "Solar activity heats Earth's atmosphere and causes it to puff outward" · "which increases drag on all spacecraft in low Earth orbit, gradually reducing their altitude over time."
"Nobody steers" = Folgerung (Quellendatei Z25); keine Kollisionszahl

scenes.text: NASA's Swift telescope had already sunk below *two hundred fifty miles*, waiting for a boost. So, ghost, how long until Earth *forgets* us? | It already started.
scenes.visual: Counter 'YEAR 1'. Swift as a cute flat telescope icon with a worried face, an altitude ruler beside it sliding down past '250 MI'. On 'forgets' Spotlight moment: everything dims, YOU center in a single beam, the question sticker returns (re-hook).
sources: Z7: "As of early February, Swift's average altitude had fallen below about 250 miles (about 400 kilometers)." · Swift-Blog: Mission "prep for orbit boost" (Seitentitel)
Re-Hook der zentralen Frage (Experiment)

scenes.text: Year ten. Our methane? Mostly scrubbed from the air within about *ten years*. And Hubble keeps sinking. Earliest re-entry: the *mid twenty-thirties*. We always used the atmosphere as an *incinerator* for old spacecraft. | Hubble's turn.
scenes.visual: Counter rolls fast to 'YEAR 10'. A methane cloud icon fades away like smoke from a candle. Hubble, flat and shiny, drifts lower over the glowing rim of Earth; on 'incinerator' the rim turns into a cartoon furnace mouth. YOU salutes.
sources: Z13: "methane is mostly scrubbed out of the air by chemical reactions within about ten years"
Z8: "Hubble is not expected to re-enter Earth's atmosphere until the mid 2030s at the earliest." · "Hubble's altitude is slowly decreasing."
Z9: "using the Earth's atmosphere as an incinerator for both the spent spacecraft and the refuse."

scenes.text: The Golden Gate Bridge is painted *continuously*, because salty air eats the steel. No painters now. | Rust takes no days off. Year fifteen. A plastic bottle in the sea stays robust for about *fifteen years*, then starts breaking down.
scenes.visual: Whip down to San Francisco, flat 2D: the red bridge, a paint bucket and roller abandoned on a cable; orange-brown rust patches grow like spreading ink. Counter 'YEAR 15'. Underwater layer: a clear bottle bobbing, a hairline crack appears on 'breaking'.
sources: Z20: "The truth is that the Bridge is painted continuously." · "The paint applied to the Bridge's steel protects it from the high salt content in the air which can cause the steel to corrode or rust."
Z24: "PETs seem to remain robust for approximately fifteen years. Afterwards, a significant decrease of the native functional groups was recorded"
Keine Zahl bis zum Brücken-Versagen, keine 450 Jahre (Quellendatei Fallen)

scenes.text: Year twenty-five. After one hundred sixteen thousand people left Chernobyl, plants and animals made *something of a comeback*, according to some studies. Nature doesn't wait for permission.
scenes.visual: Counter 'YEAR 25'. Flat 2D abandoned town square: weeds and trees grow through the pavement in stop-motion layers, a deer silhouette steps into frame, birds on a rusty sign. YOU sits on a bench, a fox glances at him, unimpressed.
sources: Z10: "the evacuation of 116,000 residents from a highly contaminated area" · "plants and animals appeared to have made something of a comeback, according to some studies."
Analogie, kein Beweis für die ganze Erde; keine Tierzahlen (Deryabina nicht abgerufen)

scenes.text: But one thing *won't* leave. Our carbon dioxide. Once it's in the air, it hangs around for three hundred to *a thousand years*. We're gone. Our exhaust? | Still here.
scenes.visual: Counter climbs 'YEAR 300' → 'YEAR 1,000'. A faint grey CO2 haze layer hangs over a green, empty planet like a ghost of its own; it barely thins. YOU waves a hand through it; it doesn't move.
sources: Z11: "Once it's added to the atmosphere, it hangs around, for a long time: between 300 to 1,000 years."
Nicht "weg nach 1.000 Jahren" (Quellendatei Fallen)

scenes.text: Year ten thousand. Mount Rushmore's granite erodes about *one inch* every ten thousand years. So the presidents lost about an inch. | Honestly? Still better skin than ours.
scenes.visual: Counter jumps to 'YEAR 10,000', progress bar nearly full. Flat 2D Mount Rushmore, four stone faces (simplified, no likeness detail), lichen and trees around; a tiny ruler shows '1 INCH'. YOU squints at the faces, then at his own see-through hand.
sources: Z21: "The granite erodes very slowly at only one inch every 10,000 years"
Herleitung: 10.000 Jahre × 1 inch/10.000 Jahre = 1 inch

scenes.text: So Earth forgets us. Slowly. But the Moon? | The Moon has no wind and no rain. Apollo tracks were still visible *thirty-nine years* later. A NASA orbiter even spotted the *shadows* of our flags.
scenes.visual: Twist, colour shift to cold silver. Match cut: YOU's round ghost head → the full Moon. Flat grey lunar surface, a trail of boot prints and rover tracks, a little flag shadow stretching across the dust. Progress bar STOPS dropping on 'Moon'.
sources: Z14: "The Moon has no atmosphere, and no wind or rain to sweep the footprints away." · "the tracks that Apollo 15 astronauts ... made 39 years previously"
Z15: "scientists can see the shadows cast by the American flags the astronauts planted at the sites."
Nicht "Millionen Jahre", nicht "Flaggen stehen noch" (Quellendatei Fallen)

scenes.text: Far out there, Voyager One left the Sun's bubble in twenty twelve, carrying a golden record. President Carter wrote it's likely to survive *a billion years*. | So our last proof? A message, flying away from an empty planet. And it all starts tonight.
scenes.visual: Pull back from the Moon past the planets to deep black space; Voyager 1 (flat icon, big dish) crosses a faint bubble line labelled 'HELIOSPHERE'. The golden record glints. On 'tonight' a form-wipe returns to the night street from the hook and the counter snaps back to 'HOUR 0' (loop).
sources: Z16: "on Aug. 25, 2012, the spacecraft became the first to exit the heliosphere" · "The probe is now in interstellar space"
Z17: "It is likely to survive a billion years into our future" (Carter, Hoffnung, keine Messung)
Kein Datum für einen anderen Stern (Quellendatei Fallen)
